pairs.question: Possum scire, quo profectus, cuius sis aut quid veneris?
pairs.answer: Huc eo, eri iussu, eius sum servos.
pairs.derivation: Mercurius interrogates Sosia. The interrogative is verbatim; Sosia's reply answers all three points (where going, whose, why). The answer ends at the first full stop; the following line ('numquid nunc es certior?') is dropped as a further taunt. The editorial supplement <iussu, eius> is rendered as its Latin words without the angle brackets.

pairs.question: Quis erus est igitur tibi?
pairs.answer: Amphitruo, qui nunc praefectust Thebanis legionibus, quicum nupta est Alcumena.
pairs.derivation: Mercurius asks who Sosia's master is; Sosia answers verbatim. Window ends at the full stop before Mercurius's next question ('Quid ais? quid nomen tibi est?').

pairs.question: quid nomen tibi est?
pairs.answer: Sosiam vocant Thebani, Davo prognatum patre.
pairs.derivation: Mercurius's 'quid nomen tibi est?' (the framing 'Quid ais?' that precedes it is dropped) is answered directly by Sosia. Window is the whole verbatim reply (one sentence).

pairs.question: quid Amphitruoni doni a Telobois datum est?
pairs.answer: Pterela rex qui potitare solitus est patera aurea.
pairs.derivation: Sosia tests the disguised Mercurius about the war-prize; the framing 'sed quid ais?' is dropped. Mercurius answers verbatim (the golden bowl). The editorial supplement <doni> is rendered as its Latin word without angle brackets.

pairs.question: ubi patera nunc est?
pairs.answer: Est in cistula; Amphitruonis obsignata signo est.
pairs.derivation: Sosia asks where the bowl is now; the framing 'Elocutus est.' is dropped. Mercurius answers verbatim. Window runs to the first full stop (covering the second clause, separated only by a semicolon). The editorial supplement <Est> is rendered without angle brackets.

pairs.question: Signi dic quid est?
pairs.derivation: Sosia asks what the seal is; Mercurius answers verbatim. The reply's following retort 'quid me captas, carnufex?' is dropped as it stops answering and turns to accusation.

pairs.question: si tu Sosia es, legiones cum pugnabant maxume, quid in tabernaclo fecisti?
pairs.answer: Cadus erat vini, inde implevi hirneam.
pairs.derivation: Sosia poses a private-knowledge test as a genuine question; setup ('si tu Sosia es... maxume') is kept verbatim so 'quid in tabernaclo fecisti?' has its frame. Mercurius answers verbatim. The intervening 'victus sum, si dixeris.' is part of Sosia's own setup line and is dropped as framing/wager, not part of the question proper; the answer window ends at the first full stop, before Sosia's aside 'Ingressust viam.'

pairs.question: Quid istuc est, mi vir, negoti, quod tu tam subito domo abeas?
pairs.answer: sed ubi summus imperator non adest ad exercitum, citius quod non facto est usus fit quam quod facto est opus.
pairs.derivation: Alcumena asks why Jupiter (as Amphitruo) leaves so suddenly. His reply opens with a non-answering deflection ('Edepol haud quod tui me neque domi distaedeat'); per the skip-the-preamble rule the answer starts at the operative 'sed ubi summus imperator...' which actually gives the reason (a commander must be with the army). Window ends at the full stop.

pairs.question: numquid vis?
pairs.derivation: Jupiter (as Amphitruo) asks the parting formula 'do you want anything?'; Alcumena answers verbatim ('Yes: that you come quickly'). The preceding 'iam ego sequar.' is Jupiter's separate remark to Sosia and is dropped as framing.

pairs.question: Quis te verberavit?
pairs.answer: Egomet memet, qui nunc sum domi.
pairs.derivation: Amphitruo asks who beat Sosia; Sosia gives the paradoxical but genuine answer 'I myself, who am now at home.' Both lines verbatim and complete.

pairs.question: Quis ad fores est?
pairs.derivation: Mercurius (on the roof, as Sosia) asks who is at the door; Amphitruo answers 'It is I.' A genuine interrogative with a direct answer.

pairs.question: Prodigum te fuisse oportet olim in adulescentia. Quidum?
pairs.answer: Quia senecta aetate a me mendicas malum.
pairs.derivation: Mercurius's taunt 'Prodigum te fuisse...' is kept verbatim as setup so Amphitruo's why-question 'Quidum?' has its referent; Mercurius answers with 'Quia...' (because in old age you beg a beating from me). A clean why/because interrogative-and-answer.

pairs.question: Quis me tenet?
pairs.derivation: The dazed Amphitruo asks who is holding him; Bromia answers 'Your maid Bromia.' Genuine interrogative, direct verbatim answer.

pairs.question: sed quid tu foras egressa es?
pairs.answer: Eadem nos formido timidas terrore impulit in aedibus, tu ubi habitas.
pairs.derivation: Amphitruo asks why Bromia has come outside; she answers that the same dread drove them out of the house. Window ends at the first full stop ('tu ubi habitas.'), before her elaboration 'nimia mira vidi...'.

pairs.question: voce clara exclamat uxorem tuam— Quis homo?
pairs.answer: Summus imperator divom atque hominum Iuppiter.
pairs.derivation: Bromia's narration 'voce clara exclamat uxorem tuam—' is kept verbatim as setup so Amphitruo's interrupting 'Quis homo?' has a referent; Bromia answers verbatim 'The supreme commander of gods and men, Jupiter.' Window ends at the full stop, before 'is se dixit...'.
